\paragraph{RAND doctor-visits application.}
The RAND Health and Retirement Study doctor-visits analysis used a deterministic smoke-profile sample of 40 subjects from 1034 eligible complete-covariate subjects (551 observed responses).
The primary model selected by joint AIC used a NBII marginal distribution with a Clayton copula and theta formula \texttt{~1} (joint AIC 2869.34).
The pre-specified covariate-dependence contrast \texttt{~wave_scaled + arthritis} was a likelihood-improving exploratory contrast rather than the AIC-preferred model: joint log likelihood changed by 0.85, AIC changed by 2.30, and the nested LR-screen p-value was 0.428.
The primary refit reported convergence as \texttt{TRUE} after 6 outer iterations, using convergence fields read directly from the fitted object.
Following the native workflow, the analysis also records data shape, missingness, time-stratified moments, pairwise dependence, screening overlays, \texttt{check\_model()}, term plots, marginal diagnostics, copula diagnostics, predictions, marginal effects, model-based simulations, and benchmark-standard-model comparisons. The compact \texttt{check\_model()} statuses were: Convergence=PASS; Marginal fit=FAIL; Tail fit=PASS; Copula fit=PASS; Variance calculation=PASS.
The associated figures report the observed doctor-visit distribution, adjacent-wave Kendall dependence, fitted covariate effects on the selected copula dependence parameter, and available marginal-parameter standard errors. Exact-discrete longitudinal standard errors use analytical rectangle-likelihood Hessians when available and are marked unavailable only when Hessian estimation is singular or intentionally skipped.
